newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: Malaysia issues alert on missing bills.
newsitem.headline: Malaysia issues alert on missing bills.

text.p: Malaysia's central bank has asked people to be on the look-out for 500-ringgit ($201) bills after the disappearance of a shipment of newly printed notes, police said on Sunday.
The bills were sent recently to the Bank Negara Malaysia, the central bank, for "approval" by its British-based printer, a police spokesman told Reuters.
A Bank Negara statement said the 500-ringgit bills, 200 of them, all bore the same serial number of ZW0000000 and had the word "contoh" (sample) printed on them.
The central bank said the matter was under police investigation and advised the public to turn in such notes if they were found.
Officials at Bank Negara were unavailable for further comment.
The disappearance of the bills was discovered early last week when a commercial bank turned over to Bank Negara a 500-ringgit note it received from a man who wanted to exchange it for smaller bills.
The commercial bank only realised later that the bill was new and had not yet been issued by Bank Negara.

Bank Negara, on learning of the incident, contacted the printer, Harrisons and Sons, who confirmed sending a batch of newly-printed 500-ringgit bills via secured courier to the central bank for approval.
